04A TECHNICAL FOUNDATION

Nuclear Engineering Background

Naval nuclear power training and submarine engineering experience across reactor physics, thermodynamics, electrical systems, and safety-critical testing. Explore how those disciplines connect in a propulsion plant.

Naval nuclear propulsion explorer
Select a system to see its role and engineering connections.

DRAG TO ROTATE · ARROW KEYS ALSO WORK
Rod motion is illustrative, not an operating control. No reactor response is simulated.

Hot leg · primary waterCold leg · primary waterHot steam · secondaryCondensed / feed waterSeawater in → out
Primary · closed circuit

Reactor → hot leg → steam-generator U-tubes → cold leg → reactor.

Pressurized water stays liquid. The illustrated coolant pumps circulate water through the primary circuit.
Secondary · closed circuit

Steam generator → turbine → condenser → feed pump → steam generator.

Steam becomes water again. It never mixes with primary coolant.
Seawater · once-through cooling

Sea inlet → condenser tubes → warmer discharge back to sea.

Seawater removes heat without mixing with steam or condensate.

Conceptual 3D educational model of a typical pressurized-water propulsion plant. Not an S8G schematic, physical layout, or operating simulation. Component geometry, positions, and quantities are illustrative; animation indicates energy flow, not measured conditions. Auxiliary equipment is omitted. The lower steam-generator bundle uses a generic inverted-U-tube arrangement with a bottom tube sheet and primary headers. Public references: NRC PWR Systems and the U.S. Navy’s public propulsion overview.
